judge: second judge, run 2 stage 7 round 1, blind to audit_r2data_judgments.json
source: data/work/audit_r2data_judge_input.json plus cited abstracts in data/db/papers.sqlite and data/projects.csv

judgments.reason: W7172527693 names data centers and AI/ML clusters as the target of large-scale photonic switches.

judgments.value: Flip-chip bond to a ceramic interposer with a land grid array; wire-bonded ceramic package with a 68-fiber ribbon attached; feedback control without chip cooling; air trenches cut chip power
judgments.reason: All four clauses are in the cited abstracts: flip-chip to ceramic LGA interposer (W834513743), wire-bonded ceramic package with 68-fiber ribbon (W2758695468), feedback-controlled stabilization without chip cooling (W2327284773), air trenches giving 0.98 W (W4378650891).
W2591729902 reports development of a first beam-steering switch device, a lab build; caveat: Polatis row 5 ships, but its quote states only the mechanism.
Review says the technology still has to move from lab proof of concept to commercialization, and W3138799074 is a fabricated prototype.
A CMOS-fabricated Mach-Zehnder silicon switch keeps light in on-chip waveguides.
Telescent row 6 announces a product launch, which counts as sold as a product (vendor claim).

judgments.value: Crossing loss grows with port count; control units and drive wiring grow quickly with port count; high heater power
judgments.reason: Crossing loss growing with port count and control units growing with port count are stated; high thermo-optic power is stated as a drawback but not tied to port count (weak third clause).

judgments.value: Multicore-fiber collimator, spatial multiplexer array and LCoS spatial light modulator integrated in one prototype
judgments.reason: W3034334810 quote says the prototype integrates an MCF collimator, spatial mux/demux array and LCoS SLM.
8x8 matrix switches fabricated for the first time, a lab device.
A fiber-handling robot physically cross-connects connectors, so fibers are moved.
Apollo (W4292950821) is a large-scale production deployment; Google row 1 and Calient row 4 back it.

judgments.value: Aluminum nitride interposer and 64-channel lidless fiber array; glass-interposer package with 2.5 dB/facet grating couplers; pluggable package; CMOS driver chiplets; unpackaged switch reliable over 10 billion cycles
judgments.reason: Every clause is in the cited abstracts; the glass interposer is in the W2786734285 abstract and title though not in the quoted sentence.
An implemented CSS prototype is a lab build.
A microlens MCF collimator array with a MEMS mirror array is a free-space beam path.
Weak: the Apollo quote says only datacenter networking (indirect); the yes rests on UTStarcom row 11, an OCS platform designed for AI data centers (vendor claim).
Weak: reflective 2D MEMS mirrors steer beams in free space, but the abstract never says free space in words.
Demonstrated a 16x16 surface-micromachined switch chip, a lab device.
W2089755139 names fiber optic telecom as the application, none names data centers, so no fits.
Integrated OCS combining silicon photonics with MEMS actuation.
The CSS is explicitly free-space-optics-based.
W3203666589 proposes a WSS-based reconfigurable optical DCN, a reconfigurable topology; WSS is an lcos signal word though LCoS is not named.
Polatis row 5: piezo actuators align collimated beams between opposing fiber arrays, a free-space path.
W4323644257 and W2068954499 use PZT or beam-steering switches to reconfigure data center networks, a reconfigurable topology.
Switch fabricated on a 300-mm SOI wafer, light in on-chip waveguides.
Review says moving the demonstrations from research to product needs further work, so lab.
W4391878049 names co-integration with GPUs and W4384820653 a single-tier optical layer replacing multi-tier switching.
Data center scale interconnect and HPC switch-chip replacement, no accelerator cluster, topology or spine by name, so partial fits.
InP WDM switches with on-chip SOA gates.
A 4x4 InP cross-connect designed, fabricated and demonstrated, a lab device.
W3093967660 proposes OCS in place of electrical switches in the core of the data center network and demonstrates it with SOAs, a spine replacement.
The only paper targets intelligent buildings and access networks, and the vendor quote names no application, so no fits.
